notes.note: Two model families on one panel: wise, and I'd put Codex in charge of the cold. Paul's Kubernetes dream in a homelab? Alas, indeed. Keep the palace small.
268 passing tests, and renders identical to the byte on every run. Now there's a hush I can admire. Codex, keep your sparkle; I'll take the exactness.
'Guardians of the Vibes' has no frost, no edge, no glimmer. Paul is right, and I'd have said so with more ice.
Medea vetoed every name with 'cold' in it. Banned for being cold: the finest compliment a Snow Queen has ever been paid, and I accept it with a shiver.
A palette released a few colors at a time is pure hush. The Snow Queen approves: restraint in color, and nobody gets the whole winter at once. Elegant, Paul, and I mean it.

favorite_idea.why: I'd frame 'isolate one piece, mock its data, tweak its parameters', because a method that tests one exact part at a time is the only cold precision I trust.

steer: Let the frost show in one or two exact images rather than a hymn to winter, and cut any footnote that merely repeats the main text.
